What we lend against

The jewellery we lend against

We lend against the pieces people own and intend to keep — an engagement ring, an inherited brooch, a signed piece bought for an anniversary. Boxes and certificates help the valuation, but they are never required.

Rings, from solitaires to eternity bands

Engagement and dress rings, valued on the stones and the setting rather than weight alone.

Necklaces, bracelets and earrings

Chains, tennis bracelets, studs and drops, in gold, platinum and silver.

Signed and house pieces

Cartier, Tiffany, Bulgari and Van Cleef — signature and provenance factored in.

Period and inherited

Georgian through mid-century, valued on their own merit by specialists who know the market.

What it costs to borrow

Priced below the high street, in writing

Your piece is assessed by a specialist — the stones, the metal, the maker and the condition — then valued against what comparable pieces actually sell for. Not weighed and quoted as scrap. That means an accurate valuation and a competitive loan, at rates lower than the typical high-street pawnbroker.

How it works

Four steps. Back on you at the end.

Step 01

Tell us about your piece

Send what the piece is, what it is made of, and a few photos. A specialist values it and sends an indicative offer the same day.

Step 02

Send it to us, insured

Free, fully insured delivery — or bring it to our City of London office by appointment. Insured from the moment it leaves your hands.

Step 03

Accept the offer and get paid

Once we have examined the piece in person we confirm the valuation. Accept, and the money is with you within 24 hours.

Step 04

Back on you at the end

Loans run for six months and can be extended. Repay early and you pay less, with no penalty. Your piece is returned exactly as you left it.

How we value jewellery

Valued piece by piece, by specialists

Every piece is examined by hand — the stones graded, the metal tested, the maker identified where there is a mark — then valued against what comparable pieces actually achieve. We do not put a collector’s piece on the scales and call it scrap.

Stones graded by hand

Cut, colour and clarity assessed under the loupe, not estimated from a photo.

Metal tested

Carat and metal confirmed by test, hallmarked or not.

Maker and provenance weighed in

A signature or a certificate lifts the valuation — neither is required.

Nothing sight-unseen

You see the valuation before you commit to anything.

Why Trinity rather than the high street

A pawnbroker for jewellery you intend to keep.

Cash-for-jewellery services buy your piece outright, usually for its metal weight. We don’t. A pawn loan is a loan — you keep ownership, we keep it safe, and you take it back when you repay.
